meta_description: Farm-to-shelf traceability on a permissioned chain — recall scope down 85% and the retailer audit passed in one walkthrough

blocks.x: Farm-to-shelf traceability on a permissioned chain, recall scope down 85% and the retailer audit passed in one walkthrough
Identity withheld, a food processing group whose recall drill assumed the worst and whose traceability couldn't say how bad the worst was. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline exercise priced the unknown: a mock recall taking 61 hours to scope, three retailer audits yearly each consuming weeks of evidence assembly, and one real allergen incident whose scope was only bounded a week after the shelves were already being cleared.
Traceability data existed at each step, farm lots, processing batches, shipments, but in systems that didn't link. The chain was a filing exercise, not a query.

We anchored the chain on a permissioned ledger: farm lots, processing events and shipments hashed and linked from field to shelf with suppliers anchoring at source, recall scoping running as a single query returning affected lots and destinations in minutes, retailer audits walking the live chain instead of reading binders, and supplier onboarding gated by anchoring quality. The filing exercise became a query.
